title: UROFACIAL SYNDROME 1
alt_titles: FACIAL PALSY, PARTIAL, WITH URINARY ABNORMALITIES
INVERTED SMILE AND OCCULT NEUROPATHIC BLADDER

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that urofacial syndrome-1 (UFS1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the HPSE2 gene (613469) on chromosome 10q24.2.

checks.claim: Urofacial syndrome-1 (UFS1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the HPSE2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous exonic deletions, nonsense mutations, and frameshift mutations in five further unrelated families confirmed HPSE2 as the causative gene for UFS.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports homozygous HPSE2 mutations as the cause of urofacial syndrome. 'UFS1' is the draft's own naming.

checks.claim: The HPSE2 gene is located on chromosome 10q24.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Previously, we localized the defective gene for the urofacial syndrome (UFS) to a region on chromosome 10q24 by homozygosity mapping.
checks.explanation: The paper places the gene at 10q24. The more precise band 10q24.2 is standard cytogenetic nomenclature that restates this location.

paragraphs.text: Urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome is a rare autosomal recessive disorder (Wang et al., 1999). It is characterized by facial grimacing when attempting to smile and by failure of the urinary bladder to void completely, despite a lack of anatomical bladder outflow obstruction or overt neurological damage (Daly et al., 2010). Patients have an unusual 'inverted' facial expression and appear to be crying when they smile (Derbent et al., 2009). Affected individuals often have reflux of infected urine from the bladder to the upper renal tract, with a risk of kidney damage and renal failure (Daly et al., 2010). The urinary problems usually result in urinary tract infection and hydronephrosis (Derbent et al., 2009). Constipation may also occur (Ochoa and Gorlin, 1987).

paragraphs.text: Ochoa and Gorlin (1987) drew attention to the association of distortion of facial expression with neuropathic bladder and resultant damage to the genitourinary tract. They recommended that individuals with 'inversion' of facial expression undergo urological evaluation. About two-thirds of their patients also had moderate to severe constipation.

paragraphs.text: Urofacial syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder (Wang et al., 1999). Ochoa and Gorlin (1987) concluded that the occurrence of the disorder in multiple sibs and increased parental consanguinity indicated autosomal recessive inheritance. The disease gene was localized by homozygosity mapping (Wang et al., 2003), and Daly et al. (2010) confirmed HPSE2 as the causative gene by identifying homozygous mutations.

checks.evidence_quote: Our previous studies using homozygosity mapping have located the UFS gene to a genomic interval of approximately 360 kb on chromosome 10q23-10q24.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the UFS gene was localized by homozygosity mapping. That mapping was done in the authors' earlier studies. This 2003 paper refined the interval to 220 kb.
